hero_h1: Put AI to work inside the tools you already use.
hero_lead: We connect AI to engineering software, office workflows and research practice, then train your people to run it. Real projects, measured results, and no hype.
svc_h2: AI for academics, professions and everyday work
svc_p: Every engagement starts from a real task you do each week. We pick the right AI tools, connect them to your files and software, and leave you with a working system and the skills to keep it running.
s1_d: AI that works directly inside your design, analysis and mapping software.
s2_d: Scheduled jobs that read your email, update your sheets and send the report.
s3_d: Responsible AI for teaching, study and research, within your institution's rules.
s4_d: Faster proposals, reports and schedules that still read like your firm wrote them.
s5_d: Small, dependable tools built around a specific calculation or system.
s6_d: Hands-on sessions so your team can use AI safely and well on its own.
proc_h2: From one weekly task to a working system
p1_d: A free call to map where time goes and which tasks AI can safely take on.
p2_d: We automate one real task end to end and measure the time saved.
p3_d: We connect it to your software, schedule it and document how it runs.
p4_d: Your team learns to run and extend it, with support when you need it.
work_p: Ten recent projects across structures, GIS, planning and automation. Client and site names are withheld.
about_p: Founded by Innocent Pius Tesha, a civil, structural and GIS engineer, Mind Freedom uses AI on live projects and measures what it saves. AI does the repetitive work; your people keep the judgement.

proc_p: We start small and prove the value on your own data before anything grows. You keep every file, script and workflow we build.
c1t: HDPE culvert encasements, validated by 3D finite element analysis
c1p: Four culvert encasement variants modelled and analysed in MIDAS Civil, with load cases, combinations and mesh checks set up through AI. The results became a reusable design workbook, Word design reports and AutoCAD drawings.
c2p: A QGIS atlas that shows what has been inspected and built on two road contracts, refreshed and exported to PDF every day at noon.
c3p: Two scheduled runs, one in the cloud and one on the office PC, read RFI emails, extract the details and keep the project sheets current.
c4t: Multi-storey car park beside a World Heritage site
c4p: From research on heritage, ground and traffic constraints to a live five-storey ArchiCAD model with a parametric parking object.
c5p: A realistic programme with overlapping trades, built and formatted inside MS Project, with A2 Gantt charts and a schedule report.
c6p: A competition entry linking planned coastal data centres to an island's freshwater and a marine conservation area, from approved data sources.
c7t: Structural model, analysis and drawing set
c7p: A multi-storey reinforced concrete building modelled, loaded and analysed in STAAD.Pro, with the drawing set finished and plotted in AutoCAD.
c8p: An Excel VBA tool that runs HDPE and PVC culvert checks, sweeps cover depths, compares sizes and flags every pass or fail.
c9p: An n8n workflow that checks inspection requests and the forecast against the road specifications, then emails each site a morning advisory.
c10t: AI connectors for desktop engineering software
c10p: AI connected to the office PC's engineering programs, so analysis, scheduling and drafting can run inside them directly.
wfiles: Drawings, reports and workbooks contain client information and are shared on request, with permission.
